title: Asymmetric mid-plane gas in ALMA images of HD 100546
question: What are the dust and gas masses, gas-to-dust ratio, azimuthal asymmetry and radial grain-size trends in the HD 100546 disc, using new Band 6 continuum, 13CO and first-detected C18O plus archival Band 7 continuum?

what.value: dust opacity kappa(1.3mm)=1.15 cm2/g for amax=1 mm, and opacity indices beta

evidence.quote: Assuming a maximum grain size $a_{\rm max}$ = 1 mm yields $\kappa_{1.3 \rm mm}$ = 1.15 $\rm cm^{2}g^{-1}$ (cite: Draine2006).
the isotopic ratio $^{13}$CO/C$^{18}$O=8 based on ISM values (cite: Wilson1999)

recipe.method: CASA 4.7.0 calibration, self-cal, CLEAN with briggs robust=0.5, uvcontsub, immoments
key_parameters: robust=0.5; channels with >3 sigma signal summed

recipe.goal: Determine geometry and centre of emission
recipe.method: Minor axis from systemic-velocity channel; elliptical Gaussian fit with PA prior for inclination; image- and uv-plane centre fits
Optically thin flux-to-mass relation within 3 sigma contour
key_parameters: T = 20-40 K; amax = 1 mm; kappa = 1.15 cm2/g

recipe.method: Optically thin LTE C18O (2-1) mass, ISM abundances, over range of T; g/d from T=20 K masses
assumptions: ISM C18O abundance, no isotope-selective photodissociation or freeze-out

recipe.method: Flux ratios of 60-degree segments on opposite sides; required density or temperature change; Toomre Q
Deproject (i=43, PA=144) and azimuthally average; noise from off-source polynomial fits; edge where flux < 2x noise

recipe.goal: Spectral and opacity index radial profile
recipe.method: Azimuthally averaged 867 um and 1.3 mm profiles, beta from d log F - d log B over d log nu

evidence.quote: The integrated continuum flux in the 1.3 mm image of 492 mJy
The $^{13}$CO (2-1) integrated flux is measured at 12.872 Jy kms$^{-1}$
an integrated flux of 2.948 Jy kms$^{-1}$ for the (2-1) transition
The average value of the two is $144\pm 2.4^\circ$ which we adopt henceforth.
We adopt an average inclination of $43^{\circ}$ for all further analysis.
giving a minimum disc gas mass of 0.018 M$_{\odot}$
we calculate a g/d for HD 100546 of $\approx$ 19
detected as far out as 385$\pm$11 au

answer_key.quantity: SW/NE brightness ratio, outer disc C18O

evidence.quote: Q(R) for this disc reaches a minimum $\sim 24$ at $\sim$80 au
begins in the inner disc with a value of 2.1 and steadily rises with radius by $\Delta \alpha_{\rm mm} \approx$ 0.3
